Comments: An unidentified pedestrian died Sunday after being struck by a Dodge Charger at Murfreesboro Pike and Summercrest Blvd around 8:30 p.m. MNPD reports the 25-year-old driver was going through a green light, showed no signs of impairment, and remained at the scene.

Austin Franklin, 24, died Sunday after grabbing the steering wheel during an argument with a 20-year-old driver on I-65 North near Briley Pkwy. The Camry veered off-road, crossed all lanes, and hit a median. Franklin died at the scene; the driver is stable at Skyline Medical Center.

Victim Names: Madisson A. De La Paz Garcia
Comments: Madisson A. De La Paz Garcia, 1, died Monday after being struck by an SUV outside her home on Murfreesboro Pike. Her aunt pulled forward, unaware the child was near the vehicle. Madisson died at Vanderbilt Children’s Hospital.  The precise location of this crash is unknown for privacy.

Motorcyclist Juan Resendiz, 25, died Saturday after colliding with a Buick Envista turning onto Walton Lane from Gallatin Pike S. Resendiz was thrown from his motorcycle and passed away at Skyline Medical Center. The investigation is ongoing.

An unidentified male driver died Friday after losing control and striking a power pole and concrete pillar on Old Hickory Blvd near Seven Springs Way. The 1:30 a.m. crash caused his car to overturn and knocked out power to the area. MNPD suspects speed was the primary factor.
Per MNPD, a fatal head-on collision occurred at this location on Dickerson Pk, near Sunset drive at 9:00 PM on Sunday, September 20th.  No further details are known at this time.

Emily C. Dollarhide, 35, died at Skyline Medical Center following a crash in the 4700 block of Ashland City Hwy. She was a passenger in a Ford Mustang that struck a pickup truck making a u-turn. Her husband was uninjured, and the truck driver sustained non-life-threatening injuries.

Savannah Stair, 28, died after her Toyota 4Runner ran off the road along a curve, hit a curb, and overturned late Friday on Great Circle Road. She passed away at Vanderbilt Medical Center. MNPD noted no signs of impairment.

Two semis and at least three passenger vehicles were involved in a crash on I-24 W in the westbound lanes near mile marker 60 (Hickory Hollow Pkwy) at 11:55 p.m. Thursday evening.  One person involved in this crash was taken to an area hospital where they died. The number of injuries is unknown.

Julio Cesar Ramirez-Rondon, 35, of Antioch died after striking parked vehicles in the parking lot of Meadowood Apartments.  MNPD officers responded shortly after 10 p.m. to find the rider unresponsive, and medics pronounced him dead at the scene.

Robert Gerald, 69, was driving a 2015 GMN Terrain when, for reasons unknown, the SUV traveled over the double yellow lines and off the roadway, where it then collided head-on into a tree.  Gerald was wearing a seatbelt and was taken to Vanderbilt University Medical Center, where he died.

Sunday morning, a 28-year-old Nashville woman died after her Ford F-150 traveled onto a curb, went up an embankment, and flipped onto its side on Murfreesboro Pike. The driver was not wearing a seatbelt and was ejected in the crash. She later passed away at Vanderbilt Medical Center.

Andre Adams, 20, died Sept. 23 from injuries sustained during a Sept. 5 street racing crash at Bomar and Centennial Blvd. Adams was ejected when a speeding Infiniti Q50 went airborne over tracks and crashed. Driver Ja’Quarius Meredith, 25, fled the scene and is wanted by MNPD.

Joseph Ballentine, 35, died Saturday after being struck by a westbound car while lying on the road in the 5700 block of River Road. The driver showed no impairment and could not avoid the impact around 2:30 a.m. along the dark, curved stretch of roadway.
Per MNPD and WKRN, a wrecker turning left onto Fesslers Lane hit a man who was walking. He reportedly died at the scene.

46-year-old Jason Gooch, of Nashville, was traveling along the I-440 exit ramp to I-24 East around noon when he lost control of his Kawasaki ZX6 during a curve.  Officials said the motorcycle went to the left shoulder before crashing into the cable barrier median.

Kendreck Murry Jr., 26, was driving his 2011 Hyundai Genesis at an extremely high rate of speed according to witnesses, when he struck the back of a Peterbilt garbage truck, causing the truck to overturn and his vehicle to catch fire. Murry died at the scene. No one else was seriously injured.

Investigators believe traffic was slowing for lane closures on the interstate due to road work. A tractor-trailer was preparing to change lanes when a Toyota Camry made a sudden lane change and struck the back of the trailer.

According to the MNPD’s preliminary investigation, the woman was sleeping underneath the semi-truck’s trailer when the semi-truck pulled out of a parking spot and she was struck by the rear tires.  Police said the semi-truck did not stop; the driver may have not known the woman was run over.

Martin Villagomez Jr., 30, was killed early Tuesday after his Nissan Altima was broadsided at Harding Place and Linbar Drive by a driver who ran a red light around 2:45 a.m. The other driver, Lizbeth Delgado Cruz, 32, faces vehicular homicide by intoxication charges upon hospital release.

An unidentified individual has died following an August 7 head-on collision involving a parked motor vehicle.  MNPD details state no adverse weather conditions and a "DARK - LIGHTED" illumination description.

An Australian tourist died and three others were injured after an 87-year-old driver ran a red light at 4th Avenue and Broadway, striking four pedestrians in the crosswalk. Two pedestrians and the driver remain in critical condition. MNPD is investigating the cause.

A pedestrian was killed on Murfreesboro Pk on Friday, July 31st. A MNPD Sergeant was traveling on the road and found the pedestrian lying in the middle of the road. The area was not well lit. The pedestrian was struck ~120 ft from the closest crosswalk, directly in front of a bus stop.

Madeline Mitchell, 29, of Clarksville, failed to slow down for traffic from an earlier semi-truck rollover crash. Mitchell's semi collided with the back of another semi, which then caused that truck to hit the back of a third semi-truck.  Mitchell died at the scene. The driver of the third semi sustained minor injuries.

Jason Bungarz-Kinney, 19, of Tullahoma, died overnight following a Wednesday evening crash on I-65 South near Dickerson Pike.  Bungarz-Kinney attempted to pass between two southbound semi-trailer trucks driving side by side and struck the rear of one trailer.

A male driver has died following a. single-vehicle crash on E Trinity Ln near Scruggs Ln. The preliminary investigation indicates the eastbound Accord failed to negotiate a curve, went off the roadway and struck a metal utility pole.  They were transported to Skyline Medical Center where he died.

Mikel Holder, 48, was struck and killed early Saturday morning on Murfreesboro Pike near Parks Retreat Drive.  The motorist remained at the scene, and reported that rain severely limited visibility, leaving no time to react.  The exact location of this crash is currently unknown.
A pedestrian was struck and killed just north of the intersection of McGavock Pike and Elm Hill Pike.  The driver fled the scene.  No further details are currently known.

Bankole Olupinla, 38, was killed Monday after attempting to turn left onto Murfreesboro Pike from Faircloth Ln, when he was hit by a Tesla traveling 70 mph in a 45 mph.  Olupinla's car was struck on the rear passenger side, causing it to spin and throwing him from the vehicle.  The speeding driver was charged with vehicular homicide via reckless conduct.

Robert Powell, 68, was killed when he was hit by two vehicles while attempting to cross Nolensville Pike in South Nashville early Monday morning. Powell was taken to an area hospital with life-threatening injuries and later died, police said.
A motor cyclist on I-40E was reported to be traveling at a high speed when they switched lanes and struck a truck.  No additional details are currently known at this time.

James Spiceland, 32, of Old Hickory, was following a single-vehicle crash at Old Hickory Boulevard and Shute Lane.  Spiceland was driving a Mazda M3 northbound around 8 p.m. when the vehicle left the roadway, traveled through a ditch, and struck a tree.  Police noted no signs of impairment at the scene.

Taramon Diane Lopez, 50, has passed away at VUMC following a June 27 collision on Lafayette St at Rep. John Lewis Way.  Lopez was struck by a Chevrolet Silverado at 11:47 pm. The driver remained at the scene to render aid, and showed no signs of impairment. Lopez succumbed to her injuries on July 2.

Quandrell Alderson, 46, was killed Saturday afternoon after his Hyundai Sonata left the roadway on Briley Parkway. The vehicle traveled into the median and struck a steel pole supporting a large roadway sign near mile marker 15.8 around 3:20 p.m. No other vehicles were involved.

Jessica F. Turner, 34, of Nashville, died Friday morning after losing control of her Kawasaki Ninja on the I-24 East entrance ramp from Harding Place.  Witnesses report Turner rode through a grassy area at a high speed before losing control on the pavement and sliding into the path of an SUV. No other injuries were reported.

Perry Kelso Foxx, 54, passed away on June 21, after his single-vehicle motorcycle crash on Wren Road in Goodlettsville on June 16th.  Foxx was riding southbound when he exited the roadway and struck a mailbox before coming to rest in a yard.

Donna Goad, 60, of Nashville, died Tuesday evening following a collision at West Trinity Lane and Whites Creek Pike. Goad was a passenger in a Honda Accord, driven by her Grandson, that struck a Chevrolet Silverado work truck after the truck's driver cut a turn short out of a driveway. No other serious injuries were reported.

William B. Scott, 35, was traveling southbound at 4:40 p.m. on his Kawasaki ZX1 when he struck the driver’s side of the Mercedes as it was crossing Hermitage Avenue from Academy Place.  Scott was transported to Vanderbilt University Medical Center where he died.

Carlos Ralpheal Lyons, 62, was killed after a speeding Ford Raptor truck drove onto the sidewalk in the 400 block of Woodland Street. The vehicle crossed into oncoming traffic, struck the pedestrian on the sidewalk, and crashed through a fence into a parking lot.

Zander Jeffcoat, 22, died Monday afternoon after his BMW X3 left the roadway and struck a light post at 8th Avenue South and Wedgewood Avenue. He was transported to Vanderbilt University Medical Center, where he passed away.

Alan J. Roncone, 66, of Clarksville, was killed Saturday morning after his Chevrolet Cruze was struck head-on by a Ford F-150 driving the wrong way on Briley Parkway.  The 17-year-old wrong-way driver faces charges of vehicular homicide by intoxication and reckless endangerment.

Talon Sewell, 18, died following a multi-vehicle crash on I-24 West near the Old Hickory Boulevard exit. Multiple others were injured in the collision, which occurred around 10:24 p.m. near mile marker 38.8 and forced a full closure of the westbound lanes for several hours.

An unidentified man was killed early Monday morning after being struck by a semi-truck near Harding Place and Donelson Pike.  MNPD reported that multiple calls were made before the incident about a man walking in and out of the road in the area.  The truck driver remained at the scene.

An unidentified pedestrian was killed Saturday night after being struck by a vehicle on I-24 East near mile marker 56. The single-vehicle crash occurred shortly after 9 p.m., forcing the closure of all eastbound lanes for several hours. No further details have been released.

Billy Ray Swaner, 58, was killed Monday afternoon after being struck by a freight truck near the intersection of Trinity Lane and Gallatin Pike. Metro Nashville Police are currently working to identify the victim and determine if they were in the roadway or on the sidewalk at the time of the collision.

Larry W. Smith, 52, died Wednesday after being hit by a Ford F-350 on 2nd Avenue North while on a bicycle. The crash occurred as the cyclist entered the roadway from the sidewalk. The driver showed no signs of impairment; authorities are investigating the circumstances of the incident.

Robert Johnston, 43, died following a head-on crash Tuesday morning after his Honda Accord crossed into oncoming traffic and struck a Dodge Charger. The 18-year-old driver of the Charger sustained only minor injuries.

Juan Marin-Ramirez, 29, was killed Thursday night in a multi-vehicle crash on I-24 East near mile marker 38. The preliminary investigation indicates a BMW 550 had slowed its speed due to entering traffic when it was rear-ended by Marin-Ramirez' Honda.

Terrance D. Whitman, 38, died Monday after his GMC Acadia crossed into oncoming traffic, struck two utility poles, and crashed into a home on Una Antioch Pike. His 36-year-old female passenger remains in critical condition.

Hershel Trotter, 66, was killed after being struck from behind while cycling on Harding Place. The driver fled the scene around 1:30 a.m. Investigators found car parts belonging to a 2016-2018 gray Nissan Altima, which might have front-end damage and a broken headlight. The exact location of this crash is unknown.
A Northeast bound drive on Bull Run Rd entered the opposing travel lane before exiting the roadway and striking a tree.  Further details aren't known at this time.

David Elliott, 59, was killed Sunday when his truck was struck head-on by William Richards, 48, who overcorrected after drifting off the road. A third truck then rear-ended Elliott’s vehicle. Richards is in critical condition and faces potential charges. Three others sustained various injuries.

Randall Abernathy Sr., 59, died Friday after his Harley collided with a Ford Escape at Nashboro Blvd. The driver, Elizabeth Hernandez, 70, reportedly turned right on red into Abernathy's path. It is unknown if Abernathy was traveling straight in a right turn only lane, or if he had the right of way.
A southbound driver on Murfreesboro Pk entered the opposing lanes and then exited the roadway.  Their vehicle hit a ditch and a utility pole.  Further details aren't known at this time.

A semi-truck driver died early Wednesday after rear-ending another tractor-trailer on I-65 North near Vietnam Veterans Parkway. The impact sparked a fire that destroyed the truck and its cargo of packages.

Leeann Julian, 47, was killed Monday in a multi-vehicle crash caused by a speeding Chevrolet Malibu. Julian was stopped for road construction when the Malibu struck her from behind, pinning her car against a box truck. The 27-year-old Malibu driver faces pending charges for reckless driving.

Yulonda Parham, 31, and Kanon Oldham, 27, were both killed early Sunday morning when a driver traveling outbound on Lafayette Street struck both pedestrians.  The male driver pulled over and fled on foot. The female registered owner of the Lexus responded to the scene to aid in the investigation.

Jaylen Breveard, 17, died Sunday morning after his Tesla Model 3 struck a concrete pole and overturned in the 3800 block of Dickerson Pike. Breveard lost control around 12:30 a.m., crossing all lanes of traffic. He was wearing a seat belt, and police found no signs of impairment.

Nicholas Anderson, 30, died Friday night after losing control of his motorcycle on Briley Parkway. Anderson veered into a ditch while navigating a curve. Police cite excessive speed as a factor. There were no signs of impairment at the scene.

Ronnie Wilson, 41, died in hospice care following a March 27 hit-and-run. The driver, Tyler Leavy, 27, was arrested after admitting he lied to police about hitting an animal. Leavy’s charges will be upgraded following Wilson's death.

Ray Padgett, 52, faces homicide charges after killing Oluwalayomi Fadero, 23 of Nashville, while driving a stolen F250 the wrong way on Murfreesboro Pike. Padgett, who has 20 prior felonies, rammed an unmarked police car before the fatal head-on collision. He is hospitalized with non-critical injuries.

Clifford Coleman, 68, died at Skyline Medical Center after being struck by a pickup truck while crossing Ewing Drive by a Dodge Dakota. A witness followed the driver, Beverly Jackson, 66, to their home. Jackson admitted to the crash and now faces upgraded charges following Coleman's death.

Jayson Braddy, 39, died Saturday after his Toyota Tundra crashed on the I-440 entrance ramp. Braddy traveling at a high speed when he failed to make a curve, causing the truck to roll. He was not wearing a seatbelt. Police are investigating to determine if impairment played a role in the crash.

James Jesse Box, 49 of Nashville, was killed on Wednesday while crossing the I-24/I-65 ramp. A driver in a Mitsubishi struck him at approximately 7:35 p.m. during heavy rain. The driver stopped immediately and showed no signs of impairment.

Two people died Sunday night following a high-speed chase on I-24 W near Harding Place. The incident began when TN Highway Patrol troopers attempted a stop and the driver fled. The ensuing pursuit ended in a fatal wreck that closed the interstate for several hours for reconstruction and cleanup.
Driver A was traveling eastbound on I-40 E before they struck the read end of Vehicle B, which had stopped due to traffic.  Further details are currently unknown.

Andrew E. Emerson, 28, died after his Harley Davidson struck a stopped pickup truck in traffic on Old Hickory Blvd. Witnesses say Emerson bypassed traffic on a sidewalk, swerved into oncoming lanes, and then rear-ended the truck. Emerson was not wearing a helmet. The truck driver was uninjured.

Naomi Mangrum, 76, died after being struck by a Honda HR-V while crossing Gallatin Pike in her wheelchair. Mangrum had the walk signal when the driver turned left into her. The driver admitted to looking at her GPS just before the impact and was charged with failure to yield the right of way.

Tom Nunnery, 77, died Sunday from injuries sustained in a March 2 crash on W. Trinity Lane. Nunnery was crossing the road around 6 a.m. when he was struck by a Nissan Altima. The 23-year-old driver remained at the scene and assisted him. No impairment was reported.

Carrie McManama, 65, died at the scene Monday after her Chevy Malibu struck a semi head-on in the 800 block of Robinson Road. McManama was traveling the wrong way in the northbound lane. A toxicology for McManama is pending.

Darius Woods, 29, died after being struck by an Acura MDX on I-40 West. Woods was standing in the left lane inspecting his disabled Dodge Journey after an initial crash. He succumbed to his injuries at VUMC. The Acura driver was hospitalized in critical condition.

Rex Heaton, 71, of Nashville, died after being hit by a a Hyundai Sonata on Gallatin Pike in East Nashville.  The pedestrian was taken to Vanderbilt University Medical Center where he died.  There was no evidence of impairment on behalf of the driver or the pedestrian at the scene.

Colby Chase, 22, has died following a Saturday evening collision near Edwin Warner Park. Chase was riding his Suzuki GSX when he struck a BMW SUV turning left out of the park. A second motorcyclist avoided the crash with minor injuries; BMW occupants were unhurt. The investigation is ongoing.

Metro Police are searching for the driver of a silver sedan that struck and killed Jerry Robinson, 77, in a crosswalk Friday night.  Robinson was hit in the 300 block of Antioch Pike around 7:30 p.m. while crossing from south to north.  The driver fled the scene.

Brent Rager II, 18, died on impact after his Kawasaki motorcycle ran a red light and struck an Infiniti SUV at Murfreesboro Pike and Summercrest Blvd.  Rager was observed speeding.  Video shows the SUV driver had a green light.  No impairment was detected for either driver.

A motorcyclist died after a Feb. 9 crash at Old Hickory Blvd and N Graycroft Ave. Witnesses say the rider was lane-splitting and ran a red light before striking a Nissan Altima turning left from N Graycroft. Originally hospitalized with life-threatening injuries, the motorcyclist has since passed.

David Lagrone, 48, died Thursday from injuries sustained in a Saturday crash. Lagrone turned his Mazda M3 in front of an oncoming Chevy Impala, causing the Chevy to flip into a creek. The Chevy's occupants were treated and released; police found no evidence of impairment.

Samantha Brady, 29, was traveling was traveling southbound on Clarksville Pike in a Nissan Altima when it appears she failed to negotiate a right turn at a high rate of speed.  Her vehicle left the right turn slip lane, hitting the intersection's signal mast in the pedestrian refuge island.

Darling Perez-Rios, 43, died after losing control of his Ford Explorer while exiting I-24 East at Haywood Lane. He struck a center wall, swerved, and flipped onto the driver's side. Perez-Rios was not wearing a seatbelt. Toxicology tests will determine if impairment was a factor.

Markeith Miller, 42, died in a two-vehicle crash around 2 a.m. on Old Hickory Blvd near Zermatt Ave. One vehicle struck a utility pole, and the victim was found deceased at the scene. Investigators are currently checking if impairment played a role in the collision.  Further information is pending.

Pamela Cruz, 26, died after her Toyota Corolla was struck by a westbound, speeding Mercedes C300 while she was turning left onto Piccadilly Row. The impact pushed her car into a Nissan Altima. Both other drivers had non-life-threatening injuries. There was no evidence of impairment at the scene.

Anthony Barrett, 54, died after his Chevy Silverado left Lebanon Pike and struck two trees Sunday evening. He was taken to Vanderbilt, where he passed away. Investigators are awaiting toxicology results to determine if impairment played a role.

Brett Davis, 44, was killed by a vehicle in the northbound lanes of I-65 near Rosa L Parks Blvd around 2:30 a.m.  MNPD reported he was sitting in the middle of the road when he was struck by a Hyundai Sonata. The Hyundai driver immediately stopped their vehicle and remained at the scene to speak with investigators.

A male pedestrian died after being struck early New Year's Day on Nolensville Pike near the I-440 East entrance. Found at 1:30 a.m. by another pedestrian, he was taken to Vanderbilt where he passed away. Police have no vehicle description yet and the victim remains unidentified.

Afriye Seegars, 23, was killed and a 24-year-old man critically injured while waiting for a rideshare outside Pecker’s Bar on Hermitage Ave. A speeding red/maroon car (possibly a Ford Mustang) struck them on the sidewalk around 1:30 a.m. Thursday and fled the scene.

Kira Phillips, 20 from Nashville, died Friday after being struck by two cars on Bell Road.  She was hit by the driver of a northbound Nissan Versa who was turning left onto Rice Road, throwing her into traffic where a second car struck her. Both drivers stayed and no impairment was found.

Elizabeth Sanchez, 49, faces vehicular homicide and child endangerment charges after a DUI crash killed her 11-year-old son. She drove into a ditch without braking, admitted to drinking, and will be arrested upon her hospital discharge.
An eastbound driver struck and killed a pedestrian crossing at 197 Haywood Lane. This is the third pedestrian fatality on Haywood Lane in 2025.

Blaise Schaeffer, 31, of Nolensville, was killed on Nolensville Pk just before Burkitt Rd while riding their bike.  The driver was speeding when they hit and ran before losing control and crashing on the shoulder of the road.  The driver and passenger exited their vehicle and fled on foot.  The passenger was detained at a nearby Taco Bell.

Semi-truck driver Bolton James Harry-Algeo, 31, of Barron, WI, died in an I-24 West crash near the I-40 split late Monday. Traffic slowed, he braked abruptly, causing steel beams on the trailer to shift forward and crush the cab.

James Byrnes, 64-year-old of Nashville, was killed Sunday at 6:30 p.m. crossing Haywood Lane, struck by eastbound Nissan Altima. The 21-year-old driver stopped and returned to the scene; he showed no impairment.  Our GPS location of the crash is approximate; details aren't clear.
A pedestrian was struck and killed by a southbound driver on Brick Church Pk near Avondale Circle.  The police report states it was not a hit and run, but further details aren't known.
Raymond Floyd, 58, died in a single-vehicle crash on I-40 West Sunday at 1:45 a.m. His Cadillac left the road, hitting a light pole and culvert. No impairment was suspected.

Aniceto Trujillo, 65, of Denair, California died after his truck rolled over on I-40 West near Briley Pkwy. A Toyota Corolla driver entering I-40 failed to negotiate the turn, drove into the side of the semi, and caused the rollover. The Corolla driver suffered non-life-threatening injuries.

Two passengers, Queen Umuhoza (19) and Francine Nyanduhura (22), were killed in a multi-vehicle hit-and-run crash on I-24 East near MM 62. A speeding red Lincoln Navigator hit a stopped Toyota Sienna, causing a chain reaction. The Navigator's driver fled on foot. Police are seeking the driver.

A female pedestrian was fatally hit by two vehicles on Brick Church Pike. A 17-year-old driver who fled was later arrested. A second driver, who initially thought he hit a pothole/mattress, found the victim under his car miles away.

A 72-year-old Hopkinsville, KY man was killed walking on I-24 West (MM 42.8) after his car broke down; he was trying to find a mile marker for a wrecker. He was struck by vehicles, and no drivers remained at the scene. Police are asking for witnesses or involved drivers to contact them.

John Love, 70, of Fairview, died in a three-vehicle crash on I-24 near Briley Pkwy. His Dodge Caravan maneuvered from the right exit lane, struck a Ram 3500, then crossed I-24 and was hit broadside by a Ford F-550. No one else was seriously hurt; no impairment was found.

Dustin McLeod, 41, of Smithville, was killed in a head-on crash on Clarksville Pike. A southbound pickup truck swerved into oncoming traffic to bypass a turning vehicle and struck McLeod’s northbound Jeep. McLeod died at the hospital; the 65-year-old pickup driver is in critical condition.

Motorcyclist Brennan Strain (29) died after his Harley Davidson, traveling northbound on Dickerson Pike, struck the passenger side of a van that pulled into his path. The van then hit a stopped truck. No impairment was found; police are investigating if speed was a factor.

A 9:15 a.m. crash on Thursday, at Trousdale and Briarwood Drive, killed two: Nicholas Moralas Gomez (22), the motorcyclist with the right of way, and pickup driver Dale Clay (37). The motorcycle struck the truck's driver's door as the truck turned. Speed is being investigated as a factor.
Details of this crash are currently unknown.  This is the third fatal crash on Dr DB Todd Jr Blvd in the past three months, and the second at this intersection.

A 62-year-old Nashville man was killed Tuesday night after being hit by an eastbound Toyota Camry on Lafayette St near Fairfield Ave. The pedestrian was crossing outside a crosswalk. The motorist reported they were unable to avoid the collision; no charges were filed.
Jared Sherrell, 35, died after his car, reportedly speeding and weaving, left the road on 4th Ave S at Rains Ave and struck a pole. No impairment was evident.

Victim Names: Maximos Ibrahim; Raafat Nassif; David Fakhory; Kerlos Toma
Comments: A 2-vehicle crash on Mt. View Rd. killed four teenagers early Sunday: Maximos Ibrahim (19), Raafat Nassif (17), David Fakhory (19), & Kerlos Toma (17). Evidence indicates their southbound Infiniti was partially in the northbound lane and travelling at a high speed. No one involved wore seatbelts.
A driver attempting a left turn on Long Hollow Pk from the I-65 South exit ramp stuck the passenger side of another vehicle.  No further details are known at this time.

67-year-old Bart Burton died after his Camry crossed into oncoming traffic, sideswiped a truck, and overturned on Old Hickory Blvd. The truck's driver had minor injuries.  None of the drivers involved showed signs of impairment, but witnesses noted the Camry was driving at high speeds.

63-year-old Ritaben Patel was killed in a two-vehicle crash at Tulip Grove and Chandler Rd early Monday. Patel was a passenger in a Mazda struck by a Dodge Ram. Both drivers claimed to have the green light; police are investigating. No impairment was found.

A southbound vehicle on Gallatin Pk N was attempting a left turn onto Anderson Rd when they collided with a northbound vehicle inside the intersection.  This crash was initially life threatening and has become fatal.  Additional details are unknown at this time.
A northbound motorcyclist on Lickton Pk left the roadway onto the right shoulder, struck a culvert and flipped.  Further details aren't known at this time.

Robert Powell (63, of Arizona) was found injured at Old Hickory Blvd and Rocky Lane around 7:25 p.m. Initially thought to be a fall, medics determined his injuries were consistent with being struck by a vehicle. Powell later died at the hospital. Police are searching for a SUV or pickup truck.

Motorcyclist Kei’vontae Dobson died after losing control of his Harley-Davidson and crashing on Hobson Pike near Wilder Drive.  Witnesses saw the motorcycle wobbling. Dobson was wearing a helmet, and speed and impairment are not believed to be factors.
One person was killed in a deadly crash involving a garbage truck and a tractor-trailer on I-24 West near Joelton at mile marker 33.6.  Further details aren't known at this time.
A pedestrian was killed crossing Bell Rd northbound at Cane Ridge Rd when they were struck by a driver attempting a left turn onto Bell Rd from Cane Ridge.

Christian Jordan, 19, of Nashville, was killed in a high-speed motorcycle crash on I-40 West near White Bridge Pike around 11:30 p.m. Sunday. The preliminary investigation suggests his BMW motorcycle entered a high-speed wobble and he was thrown off.

Elliot Carter, 31, was killed Thursday at 9 p.m. in a collision on Trinity Lane near Scruggs Lane. Carter's motorcycle, which was traveling at an extremely high rate of speed, struck the passenger side of a Mazda as the car was making a left turn into a parking lot.

Mack Tyrone Cosby, 50, of Nashville, was killed in a fatal hit-and-run around 10:35 p.m. Tuesday on Dr. D.B. Todd Jr. Blvd near Osage St. in North Nashville. Police are searching for the driver of a dark SUV that hit the man while he was walking on the east side of the street and then fled.
An Eastbound driver on Old Hickory Blvd was in the center turn lane to turn onto Ronnie Rd.  They were struck by a westbound vehicle in an offset head-on collision.

Patricia Owens (64), was fatally struck by a WeGo bus while crossing Dickerson Pike near Ewing Drive Wednesday at 8:30 p.m. A second pedestrian sustained non-life-threatening injuries. The bus driver attempted to swerve but hit the two people.

I-24 E near the Davidson/Rutherford County line was shut down early Wednesday after a deadly crash involving an unoccupied semi, a Chevy Silverado, and a tractor-trailer around 2 a.m. The Silverado driver, Hector Rodriguez Banuelos, was killed after hitting the semi, which was blocking lanes.

Jerry Crutcher, 67, was struck by a black Jeep on Dr. D.B. Todd Jr. Boulevard.  Crutcher died in a hospital shortly after. Police said Crutcher was lying in the middle of the road at the time of the crash.

Driver A was eastbound on Broadmoor when they ran the all-way stop sign and struck vehicle B in the intersection with Saunders Ave.  Driver B was pregnant at the time and ended up losing the child as a result of the crash.

Kyree Hollins, 26, of Antioch, died following Tuesday’s 4 a.m. head-on crash with a GMC Terrain on Bell Road at Ned Shelton Road. The preliminary investigation indicates Hollins' southbound Rogue crossed over the double yellow line where it collided with the northbound Terrain.

A motorcyclist, Kaden Chapman, 23, died after a crash with a Toyota Yaris on Korean Veterans Boulevard at 4th Ave S. The Yaris driver, 22, was cited for failing to yield after turning in front of Chapman's motorcycle, causing the fatal collision.

A 36-year-old motorcyclist, C.W. Smith, died after hitting a Toyota Rav4 on Gallatin Pike South. The Toyota was turning into a parking lot when the crash occurred. Smith was transported to the hospital where he later died.

A 15-year-old Brentwood teen, Cheathan Babu, died after a crash on Old Hickory Boulevard. Police said he was on an electric motorcycle, traveling at high speeds on the sidewalk before losing control and hitting a fire hydrant.

Terrell Robins Jr. of Elizabethtown, KY, struck the rear of a Nissan Versa on his motorcycle. The impact caused the Versa's driver to lose control and hit a second motorcycle, a Honda.  Robins was transported to VUMC, where he died. The second motorcyclist, Armando Zavala, has also died as a result of his injuries.

Nashville police are searching for a dark-colored Dodge Charger that fatally struck Lha Tun, 32, on Haywood Lane near Hopedale Dr on Thursday night. The vehicle has significant damage to its driver’s side. Tun died at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

Nicholas Leonhardt, from North Carolina, was crossing Fourth Ave S with a friend when he was hit by a blue Honda CRV in the southbound lane.  On Sunday, Sept. 14, Metro police announced that Leonhardt died as a result of his injuries.

James C. Sellars, 33, of Hendersonville, was killed Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. when his Kawasaki was rear-ended at a red light by a silver Mercedes SUV on Old Hickory Blvd. The SUV, missing its front bumper, fled south. Tips: call Crime Stoppers at 615-742-7463.

Daniel Velasco-Reyes & Mariana Maldonado-Vergara, both 19, died after their bike collided with an SUV on Nolensville Pike. Police say the SUV pulled out of a gas station lot, and the motorcycle was speeding, causing it to crash into the SUV's rear driver-side door.

A 17-year-old, Darryl Anthony, died from injuries after his ATV ran a red light and crashed into an SUV in Nashville on August 11. Neither Anthony nor his 16-year-old passenger were wearing helmets. The passenger had non-life-threatening injuries.

A Maserati driver, Julio Ceasar Herrera Gonzalez, is facing multiple charges, including vehicular homicide and DUI, after crossing into oncoming traffic on Bell Road. The head-on collision killed Raquel Lorena Sarabia Barajas, 37, in a Nissan Rogue passenger seat and left its driver with life-threatening injuries.

A tractor-trailer rear-ended a Hyundai Elantra on I-40 West in Nashville early Saturday, killing the Elantra's driver, 63-year-old Dennis E. Crowder. The crash occurred around 2:25 a.m. near the Highway 70 South exit, where traffic was already congested from a separate incident.

Joshua Parsons, a 44-year-old motorcyclist from Nashville, was killed in a collision on Gallatin Pike. The crash occurred when he collided with a Honda Pilot turning into the Target parking lot, and while the investigation is ongoing, his friends reported he was impaired and they had tried to take his keys.

Daryus Chambers, 37, of Antioch, and another motorcyclist were traveling north on I-65 at 10:45 p.m. when Chambers, it is believed, struck a tractor-trailer. He lost control and crashed on the interstate. The second motorcycle ran over Chambers, causing that 18-year-old rider to also crash. Chambers died at the scene.

Side Street: Dr Martin Luther King Jr Blvd
Comments: James D. Galloway, Jr, 73 of Nashville, died after being struck by an SUV at the intersection of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard and 10th Avenue North. Preliminary investigations suggest he stumbled into the roadway while walking, and a Lexus SUV making a right turn subsequently hit him.

Rustin Needer, 41, of Nashville was walking in the roadway when he was struck by the driver of a northbound Buick Encore.  Fatal crash investigators learned from a family member that Needer had called to say he was walking home after his vehicle broke down on Gallatin Pike near Briley Parkway.

Melena Sanderson, 42, of Nashville was fatally struck on I-40 West near Old Hickory Boulevard after exiting a gray SUV and walking into traffic. She was hit by a burgundy sedan that fled the scene, followed by several other vehicles, and the SUV she exited also left the scene.
Driver A was heading eastbound on Harding Pike, reportedly weaving in and out of traffic, when they crossed a double-yellow center lines and struck vehicle B in a head-on collision.

On Monday, July 14th, Joyce Poole was fatally injured in a three-vehicle crash on I-40 West near mile marker 213.6 when her Honda Civic struck a stopped Tesla Y, pushing it into a Chevrolet Tahoe. Ms. Poole, who was transported to Vanderbilt Medical Center, was later pronounced deceased, and no charges are expected.

Matthew Sparks, 42, of Nashville, was traveling south in his Renegade when he failed to negotiate a slight curve, crossed the double yellow lines into opposing lanes of traffic and left the roadway. The Renegade went into the woods and ultimately crashed head-on into a tree.
Multi-vehicle crash involving 9 individuals.

Julie Savoy, 53, who was critically injured in a July 8 hit-and-run at South 5th Street and Main Street, has died from her injuries. The black Hyundai Elantra involved was reported stolen after the incident, and authorities are still working to identify the driver.

10-year-old Dsiyahn Whitmore of Nashville tragically died after the gasoline-powered minibike he was riding collided with a gasoline tanker truck on Main Street. Preliminary investigations suggest Whitmore rode out of a market parking lot and into the truck's path, failing to yield, and was subsequently run over.

Kenneth Fulson, 67, died in a single-vehicle crash on John A. Merritt Boulevard on TSU's campus. Fulson's Cadillac CTS reportedly went through a stop sign at 60 miles per hour, striking a water main structure and a brick wall. Toxicology tests are pending to determine if impairment was a factor in the fatal crash.

Daniel Poole, 19, of Orlinda, was killed after his motorcycle was sideswiped by a Honda Accord exiting a parking lot on Gallatin Pike and then struck by two additional vehicles. The crash was caused by the Honda driver’s failure to yield while attempting to cross the roadway.

Robert Crawford III, 20, of Old Hickory, was killed in a head-on collision on Brick Church Pike after an 18-year-old Mississippi driver, Joshua McNeal, attempted to pass vehicles at high speed and lost control of his pickup truck. McNeal has been charged with vehicular homicide by reckless conduct and other related offenses following the crash.

Jackson Hunter, 47, of Watertown, was killed Sunday when his speeding Chevrolet Silverado ran a red light on Thompson Lane and collided with a Honda Accord; he was ejected from the truck and died at the scene. The Honda driver, who had the green light, showed no signs of impairment, and toxicology tests are pending for Hunter.

Angela Dawn Loupe, 51, of Murfreesboro, was killed in a four-vehicle crash early Sunday on I-24 East near Bell Road; John Baudendistel, 28, is charged with vehicular homicide by intoxication after rear-ending her Nissan Sentra. Two other drivers involved fled on foot after an initial collision, and police are seeking information on them as the investigation continues.

Lorenzo Mendoza, 63, was struck and killed while crossing Murfreesboro Pike early Saturday; the Medical Examiner is working to confirm his identity. Preliminary reports indicate he was hit between intersections with crosswalks near a bus stop by an eastbound Ford Escape whose driver stopped and showed no signs of impairment.

The preliminary investigation indicates the Nissan was traveling west when, for an unknown reason, it went across the eastbound lanes, left the roadway, went down an embankment and struck a utility pole.

Reana Ibrahim, 22, was driving a Mazda 3 in the wrong lane on Spring Street when she struck a Ford Bronco head-on. Her passenger, Jaiden Smith, 21, suffered critical injuries and later died on November 11, 2025. Toxicology tests revealed Ibrahim was inebriated at the time of the crash.

A 44-year-old male pedestrian died after being struck by a southbound Dodge Caravan Tuesday night on Murfreesboro Pike near Edge O Lake Drive. The driver remained at the scene, showed no signs of impairment, and authorities are working to notify the victim’s family.
Nicolas Sente Rodriguez, 27, died in a single-vehicle crash on East Thompson Lane at 8:35 p.m. on Sunday. The Ford Mustang he was driving lost control at a slight curve and hit a concrete barrier.

A pedestrian, 77-year-old Dorothy Dobbins, was killed on 3rd Avenue North near Van Buren Street when struck by a Chevrolet Silverado around 7:30 p.m. Dobbins was reportedly in a marked crosswalk at the time. She was taken to Vanderbilt University Medical Center, where she later died.

Rodrigo Vences-Dealmonte, 18, of an Infiniti M37 has died as a result of Thursday’s 9 p.m. crash on Anderson Road. The preliminary investigation indicates the Infiniti was observed street racing with another vehicle when officers attempted to stop their dangerous driving.

Larissa Houston, 23, of Nashville, was killed in a hit-and-run crash while riding her electric bicycle on Bell Road. The dark-colored sedan that struck her fled the scene at a high speed, running multiple red lights, and was last seen near the I-24 and Bell Road interchange.
Jose Salamanca, a 43-year-old from Nashville, was fatally injured on Wednesday night when he was hit by a Dodge Challenger while attempting to cross Antioch Pike at Luna Drive.

Chance Lee Kimbro, 17, was driving a stolen 2015 Ford Fusion west on I-40 when they hit a semi-trailer and were ejected onto the Interstate, and then struck by another vehicle. An unidentified passenger fled before police arrived.

Driver exited the roadway and struck a tree.  It it unclear it if was a fatal crash or a medical episode.
Little information is known about this, including the location on Granny White Pike.  This coordinate position was chosen at random.

Ashley Sells was arrested for vehicular homicide after video evidence surfaced showing her driving a car with her friend, Shannon Kilgore, on the hood. Kilgore fell and suffered a fatal skull fracture while Sells was doing donuts in a parking lot, and Sells is accused of lying to police about the incident.

The preliminary investigation shows that a pickup truck had just pulled out of the Wal-Mart parking lot to turn left (east) on Lebanon Pike when a westbound motorcycle collided with the driver’s side rear of the vehicle.

The preliminary investigation indicates that Roberta Osgood, 30, was driving her 2017 Toyota Highlander west on Old Hickory Boulevard when she traveled off the roadway, stuck a concrete mailbox, and then collided with a tree.

Kimberly Odell, 56, of LaVergne, was killed following a two-vehicle collision at the I-40 East entrance ramp on Donelson Pike. Odell was the front-seat passenger in a Mercury Mystique that was struck on the passenger side by a speeding Chevrolet Silverado.
Driver was traveling south on Dickerson Pk when they exited the roadway on the right shoulder and struck a utility pole.

Tyler S. Davis, 27, of Nashville, lost his life Friday afternoon following a collision on Lebanon Pike at Wellington Square. Davis was traveling eastbound on his Kawasaki ZX6 when he struck the driver’s side of a Nissan Frontier pulling out from a local gym.

Pritam “Peter” Singh, 42, died April 9 after the Nissan Altima he was riding in struck a semi-truck and rolled into a tree line. The driver, Inderjit Singh, was reportedly speeding at over 100 mph. He is jailed on charges of vehicular homicide and reckless endangerment.
The preliminary investigation shows that Cordae Robison, 24, of Goodlettsville, was driving west on Murfreesboro Pike when he lost control of the car in the intersection and struck a utility pole.

Kirk Granfors, 64, and Kathy Granfors, 68, of Florida, were killed when a stolen Jeep struck their taxi. Witnesses say the taxi had the green light. The Jeep's suspected driver, George Chaney, was on parole and out on bond for prior auto theft charges. Charges are pending.

Robert L. Jones, 39, was attempting to cross Trinity Lane at the light where the exit ramp from I-65 North intersects with Trinity Lane when he was struck. He was transported to Skyline Medical Center where he died.

Paula Moore, 43, of Nashville, died Thursday following a head-on collision on Old Hickory Boulevard. Her 3-year-old daughter was critically injured, and two teens were also hurt. Investigation continues to determine why one vehicle crossed the double yellow line.
Jill Edmondson, 66, and her son, Corey Vondohlen, 41, died Monday night after their Kia Optima struck a utility pole. Edmondson died at the scene, and Vondohlen later passed at the hospital.

Derrick P. Borchardt II, 22, was driving erratically and changing lanes across the interstate. The vehicle traveled to the far right of the roadway, quickly went back to the left, and struck a rock wall. It then rolled over and came to rest on the passenger side.  There were open alcohol containers in the SUV, and the passenger said they had been drinking prior to the crash.

Ronald Botts, 37, was driving west on Hart Lane when it appears that he was attempting to enter the southbound ramp to Ellington Parkway but failed to negotiate the turn due to speed, striking a rock wall.

Victim Names: Robin Bernard; Andy O. Hernandez; Jonathan J. Palafox-Pacheco
Comments: A 70-year-old driver, Robin Bernard, lost control of his vehicle on Whites Creek Pike, crossing into oncoming traffic and causing a three-vehicle collision that resulted in the deaths of Andy O. Hernandez and Jonathan J. Palafox-Pacheco, the backseat passengers. Bernard himself sustained life-threatening injuries.

Bradley Parrott, 45, and William Parrott, 72, a father and son from Illinois, were killed early today when a Ram 2500 struck their Silverado from behind at a high speed. Daniel Caravaca-Bonilla faces vehicular homicide and DUI charges; investigators found open alcohol containers in his truck.

Michael Capps (65) died in a head-on crash on Whites Creek Pike involving a semi-truck and two passenger vehicles. The semi hit Capps' Kia Forte, which then hit a Nissan Sentra. The drivers of the semi and Nissan were unhurt.

Karla Armendariz, 25, faces vehicular homicide and DUI charges for the hit-and-run death of Charles Fountain, 65. Fountain, a truck driver on his electric scooter, was struck and dragged over 900 feet by a Toyota Tundra on Old Hickory Blvd.

Armendariz fled the scene but surrendered after a Crime Stoppers tip led police to her truck. She admitted to drinking six beers and taking prescription drugs prior to the crash, claiming she "blacked out" and did not remember the collision. She was also driving without a license.

Shemica Shaunte E. Sales, 37, died Sunday morning after her Nissan Murano left the roadway and struck a brick wall and culvert. Investigations indicate the vehicle was traveling at a high rate of speed at the time. Toxicology tests are pending to determine if impairment played a role.
Caleb LeQuire, 23, was travelling westward on Elm Hill Pike when a van turned out in front of him.  He died a week later from his injuries.

Nicholas Hardy, 50, was driving an Impala northbound at a high rate of speed when it crossed into oncoming lanes of traffic before striking a metal utility pole. There were no signs of impairment at the scene.

The preliminary investigation indicates Austin Harrison, 25, was traveling between the two outbound lanes at a high rate of speed when the Honda, which was facing inbound, was making a left turn on the green light without the green left arrow.

The preliminary investigation indicates Marco Macias, 23, of Nashville, was traveling south at a high rate of speed when it struck a Chevrolet Silverado that was entering the roadway from a parking lot.  The motorcycle then crossed the road and struck the front of a northbound Jeep Compass.

The preliminary investigation indicates the Harley Davidson FLT, driven by Derek McIntosh, 36, of Smithville, was merging onto I-24 East from Harding Place when he struck the side of a tractor trailer.
Brian Morwood, 48, of Goodlettsville, was traveling southbound on Knight Valley Drive when, for an unknown reason, left the roadway and struck a tree head-on.

Gerald Edgman, 73, of Paris, Tennessee, died Friday after his Toyota Camry struck a Ford F-150 from behind and overturned. The crash occurred near McCrory Lane as traffic slowed for an upcoming construction zone. Edgman’s passenger sustained non-life-threatening injuries.

Koriona Harding, 21, of Smyrna, was killed Tuesday night while on foot near her disabled vehicle. Harding was struck by a Honda CRV after another driver swerved to avoid her. The driver of the Honda remained at the scene; no charges were filed.
Orin Odom, 78m was driving northeast on Highway 100 when he likely suffered a medical event.  His Nissan Versa veered off the road and crash head-on into a tree.

Driver A was traveling westbound on Murfreesboro Pk and attempting a left turn into the Shell gas station before the intersection of Pineway Dr when they were struck on the passenger side by an eastbound motorcyclist. The motorcyclist sustained fatal injuries.

Driver was attempting a left turn from Buena Vista Pike to continue northward on Buena Vista at the intersection with W Trinity Ln when they were struck by vehicle B westbound on W Trinity Ln.

Two passengers, including a 10 year old, were riding northbound on an electric scooter in the southbound bike lane when they were struck by a speeding vehicle in the bike lane. The child sustained fatal injuries while the adult has life threatening injuries.

Driver A was speeding down Mrufreesboro Pk when they entered a dedicated right turn lane and drove through the intersection with Morris Gentry. The driver then hit the curb on the other side of the intersection and went airborne.

Driver was traveling south on Lucas Ln when they struck a truck driver-turned-pedestrian who had just exited their vehicle parked on the east side of the road and was crossing to the gas station on the west side.
